Q: Why am I getting this error - "A character operand was found in the %EVAL function or %IF condition where a numeric operand is required." A:

Why %ELSE %DO; inside a macro call argument causes "character operand found where numeric operand required"

The short answer

The semicolon in %else %do; is leaking into the text of the argument being passed to the macro, so instead of receiving 201312, the called macro receives something like ; 201312, which %EVAL cannot interpret as a number.

Step by step explanation

Step 1: How macro call arguments are delimited

When the SAS macro processor scans a macro call like:

%looper_ccbeh(arg1, arg2, arg3)

the delimiters that separate and terminate argument values are commas and the closing parenthesis. A semicolon is not a delimiter in this context. This is stated explicitly in the SAS Macro Language Reference (%MACRO statement documentation):

"In the macro invocation, all text up to the comma is the value of parameter VAR; text following the comma is the value of parameter SUM."

Source: https://www.sfu.ca/sasdoc/sashtml/macro/zro-stmt.htm

This means that anything between the commas — including any text generated by macro statements executing during argument scanning — becomes the literal value of that argument.

Step 2: %DO and %IF-%THEN/%ELSE are "macro definitions only" statements

The SAS Macro Language Reference explicitly divides macro statements into two categories. The first category can be used anywhere (open code or inside a macro definition). The second category is restricted to macro definitions only. From the official docs:

Macro Language Statements Used in Macro Definitions Only

  • %DO
  • %END
  • %IF-%THEN/%ELSE
  • (and others)

Source: https://support.sas.com/documentation/cdl/en/mcrolref/61885/HTML/default/a001072448.htm

The argument list of a macro call is not the body of a macro definition. So when you write:

%looper_ccbeh(20&yymm.,
    %if %sysfunc(month("&report_date."d)) = 6 %then %do; 
        201406
    %end;
    %else %do;
        201312
    %end;
    ,&loopyr.)

you are using %DO/%END outside of a macro definition body — which is explicitly unsupported territory.

Step 3: What actually goes wrong

Because %DO is being used in an unsupported context, its terminating semicolons are not cleanly consumed as macro statement terminators the way they would be inside a definition body. Instead, they get emitted as literal text into the argument value being assembled. The second argument resolves to something like ; 201312 rather than the intended 201312.

This was confirmed by the OP in comments: "the macro parameter resolved to '; 202312' or something similar when month was 12."

I must conclude that the else branch when hit ALWAYS causes that problem because of the reasons explained above.

But to be fair most of this analysis is just based on the assumptions that since %IF-%THEN/%ELSE and %DO are documented as instructions supported only in macro definition body, and OP said that when %ELSE% is hit, the returned value contains a leading ;, that must be the reason for this odd behaviour.

Step 4: Why %EVAL then fails

The same SAS docs page also notes:

"Some macro statements perform an operation based on an evaluation of an arithmetic or logical expression. They perform the evaluation by automatically calling the %EVAL function." %IF expression %THEN action; is one of these statements.

So when the called macro internally uses %IF or any arithmetic on that second parameter, %EVAL is invoked automatically. It receives ; 201312 instead of 201312, sees a non-numeric token, and throws:

ERROR: A character operand was found in the %EVAL function or %IF condition where a numeric operand is required.

The fix

Replace %if/%then/%do/%end with the inline %then value; %else value; form, which does not involve %DO at all:

%looper_ccbeh(20&yymm.,
    %if %sysfunc(month("&report_date."d)) = 6 %then 201406;
    %else 201312;
    ,&loopyr.)

This uses only %IF-%THEN/%ELSE without %DO/%END. While %IF-%THEN/%ELSE is also technically a macro-definition-only statement, in the single-value inline form it does not emit any stray semicolons into the argument text — the semicolons here terminate the %THEN and %ELSE clauses cleanly, and only the bare value (201406 or 201312) is passed as the argument.

Alternatively, compute the value before the call:

%let myval = %if %sysfunc(month("&report_date."d)) = 6 %then 201406;
             %else 201312;;
%looper_ccbeh(20&yymm., &myval., &loopyr.)

This moves the conditional logic entirely outside the argument list and avoids the problem altogether.

But since we are still using %if %then %else despite we said above that they should be used only in macro definition body, and it's maybe working just because we stripped off the %do %end part, an even safer approach would be:

%if %sysfunc(month("&report_date."d)) = 6 %then %let myval = 201406;
%else %let myval = 201312;
%looper_ccbeh(20&yymm., &myval., &loopyr.)

An alternative

To perform that same logic we don't need %if at all. You can compute the value purely with %sysfunc and arithmetic, staying completely away from any macro-definition-only statements:

%let myval = %sysfunc(ifc(%sysfunc(month("&report_date."d)) = 6, 201406, 201312));
%looper_ccbeh(20&yymm., &myval., &loopyr.)

Q: How to safely construct dynamic cypher query with parameters in pl/pgsql when using apache AGE on PolarDB for PostgreSQL? A:

Where might the problem lie?

  1. You can cast props jsonb to text which makes it acceptable agtype input and output through agtype_to_text() and text_to_agtype(), but that doesn't make it compatible with Apache AGE Cypher query syntax where keys should not be quoted.
  2. The label_name got double-quoted by the %I format placeholder, which should also be reported as an error. In my tests on AGE 1.7, that's what the parser complains about. After fixing that, I'm getting a complaint about "age" being quoted, and it's the first key in there after jsonb key reordering.

I know AGE's cypher( ) function does not support parameterized queries (like $1, $2), so I can’t pass values safely as bind parameters… Any workarounds for the lack of parameterization in cypher()?

AGE does support parameterised queries with $ syntax, although only in prepared statements.

Are there community patterns for building a safe, reusable graph operation abstraction layer on top of AGE?

Prepared Statements, PL/pgSQL Functions: Dynamic Cypher. Prepared statements are tied to, and only usable by the session that allocated them, so to make them shareable, you need to wrap the prepared statement declaration and execution in a PL/pgSQL routine, which means working around a few collisions and restrictions: demo at db<>fiddle

  1. Prepared statement $ param notation clashes with the wrapping function's own $ notation: 
    create function f(f_arg agtype)returns agtype as $f$
  prepare ps(agtype) as
  select $1;--1st param of the prepared statement, not f_arg
  select $1;--f_arg, since this line is outside the `prepare`
$f$ language sql;
    In your case it isn't really an obstacle, but it's good to keep that in mind.
  2. PL/pgSQL execute runs dynamic queries, not prepared statements. That's not directly available in that context, so you need to wrap a SQL execute inside a PL/pgSQL execute. 
    create function sql_execute_vs_plpgsql_execute()returns agtype as $f$
declare ps text; r1 text; r2 text;
begin
ps := $$select 'dynamic SQL result'$$;
prepare ps as select 'prep statement result';--f_arg
execute ps into r1;--dynamic SQL execution, uses the `ps` variable, not the `ps` prepared statement
execute 'execute ps' into r2;--prepared statement execution, inside dynamic SQL
return agtype_build_map('r1',r1,'r2',r2);
end $f$ language plpgsql;
  3. There is no if not exists clause for prepare, which means you need to emulate that by either trying to prepare then catching and ignoring an error if it turns out the statement had already been allocated, or check the system catalogs and only conditionally allocate it, if it doesn't exist yet. 
    create or replace function create_node_dynamic(
    graph_name text,
    label_name text,
    props JSONB
) returns agtype as $f$
declare result agtype;
begin
if exists(select from pg_prepared_statements
          where name ~* 'create_node_dynamic')
  then deallocate create_node_dynamic;
end if;
execute format($e$
  prepare create_node_dynamic(agtype) as
    select * 
    from cypher( $gn$%1$s$gn$
                ,$q$create (n:%2$s {name: $name, age: $age}) return n$q$
                ,$1 ) as (n agtype);
    execute create_node_dynamic(%3$L);
    $e$,graph_name,label_name,props::text
  ) into result;
return result;
end; $f$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

In that context, cypher() requires that the first 2 arguments, graph_name and query_string, both have to be constants, the 2nd one dollar-quoted. A plain %L literal placeholder resulting in single quotes will be rejected with an error when the prepare gets evaluated, at runtime of your wrapper function:

ERROR:  a name constant is expected
LINE 3: from cypher( $1,$2,$3 ) as (n agtype)
                     ^

ERROR:  a dollar-quoted string constant is expected
LINE 3: from cypher( 'graphname',$2,$3 ) as (n agtype)
                                 ^

ERROR:  a dollar-quoted string constant is expected
LINE 3: from cypher( 'graphname'::name,format('create (n:%s $props) ...
                                      ^

The 3rd argument, parameters cannot replace the whole property map, like you wanted it to. It can only supply values to individual keys that need to be already in the query_string:

ERROR:  properties in a CREATE clause as a parameter is not supported
LINE 5:                     ,$q$create (n:User $props) return n$q$
                                               ^

Pretty much the only thing you can do there is offer it a $1, so any and all processing of what ends up passed into it as that parameter has to be done beforehand.
Postgres jsonpath functions are restricted the exact same way - whenever a function accepts an optional vars parameter map, it can't be used to inject actual logic, only values to be compared with. To side-step these restrictions, you need to set up your own agtype-to-cypher-query-propmap converter:

create function jsonb_to_cypher_propmap(jsonb)returns text as $f$
select '{'||string_agg( format( '`%s`:%s'
                               ,replace(k,'`','``')--escape backticks
                               ,case when jsonb_typeof(v) in('number','boolean','null')
                                     then v#>>'{}'--leave unquoted
                                     else v::text --keep JSON's double quotes
                                end)
                        ,',')
        ||'}'
from jsonb_each($1)as jbe(k,v);
$f$ language sql;
create function agtype_to_cypher_propmap(agtype)
  returns text return jsonb_to_cypher_propmap($1);

That lets you handle it fully with the 2-param cypher(), no prepared statements.

create or replace function create_node_dynamic(
    graph_name text,
    label_name text,
    props JSONB
) returns agtype as $f$
declare result agtype;
begin
execute format($e$
  select * 
  from cypher( %1$L
              ,$q$create (n:%2$s %3$s) return n$q$) 
       as r(n agtype);
  $e$,graph_name,label_name,jsonb_to_cypher_propmap(props)
  ) into result;
return result;
end; $f$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

I'm not doing anything about the label_name - at least as of v1.7, Apache AGE doesn't support whitespace or leading numerics in them, even if you quote them with backticks, so adding them doesn't protect it against users not following label naming conventions.

Q: My code is very long. Is there a way to shorten it? A:

You can use f-strings for print(zone + subzone) instead of joining 2 strings, of which 1 has a space at the begining:

print(f"{zone} {subzone}")

Q: How do I change the default value of a dropdown field based on a button in Power Apps? A:

You will also have to populate the "DefaultSelectedItems" property in your ComboBox and the way you populate will depend on how the Record of your ComboBox looks like.

It's common that you will have to do something like this for the "DefaultSelectedItems":

DefaultSelectedItems: {Value:variable} //in your case variable will be value

Q: PHP Startup: Unable to load dynamic library 'php_curl.dll' A:

I think there's something wrong with the PHP 7.2.5 installation zip (php-7.2.5-Win32-VC15-x64.zip) maybe it's the same with the 7.2.4, there are no libeay32.dll and ssleay32.dll libraries included which are obviously needed by the curl library module.

My solution was to install the 7.1.17 version where the files where included and copy those dll's to Apache bin's directory. It should be enough, if not try also to include PHP (in my case c:\usr\php71) and Apache bin (in my case c:\usr\Apache24\bin) directory to you PATH variable.. and restart Windows to be safe.

Q: ORA-19202: Error occurred in XML processing LPX-00210: expected '<' instead of 'M' Error at line 1 A:

I have faced the same issue and I was able to solve that by correcting the Xpath within the extractvalue() function. I have entered a wrong Xpath for the CLOB value extraction. Hope this might be help full to solve your problem.

Q: Importing multiple text files into the same sheet A:

You can use GetOpenFilename excel property like this:

Sub Sample()

Dim myfiles
Dim i As Integer

myfiles = Application.GetOpenFilename(filefilter:="CSV Files (*.csv), *.csv", MultiSelect:=True)

If Not IsEmpty(myfiles) Then
    For i = LBound(myfiles) To UBound(myfiles)
         With ActiveSheet.QueryTables.Add(Connection:= _
            "TEXT;" & myfiles(i), Destination:=Range("A" & Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Offset(1, 0))
            .Name = "Sample"
            .FieldNames = False
            .RowNumbers = False
            .FillAdjacentFormulas = False
            .PreserveFormatting = True
            .RefreshOnFileOpen = True
            .RefreshStyle = xlInsertDeleteCells
            .SavePassword = False
            .SaveData = True
            .AdjustColumnWidth = True
            .RefreshPeriod = 0
            .TextFilePromptOnRefresh = False
            .TextFilePlatform = 437
            .TextFileStartRow = 1
            .TextFileParseType = xlDelimited
            .TextFileTextQualifier = xlTextQualifierDoubleQuote
            .TextFileConsecutiveDelimiter = True
            .TextFileTabDelimiter = False
            .TextFileSemicolonDelimiter = False
            .TextFileCommaDelimiter = False
            .TextFileSpaceDelimiter = True
            .TextFileColumnDataTypes = Array(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
            .TextFileTrailingMinusNumbers = True
            .Refresh BackgroundQuery:=False
        End With
    Next i
Else
    MsgBox "No File Selected"
End If

End Sub

Hope this works for you.
